name: Specific Model Architectures and Extensions
text:
# Specific Model Architectures and Extensions

Also called: NSVF Model Architectures

## Overview
This family defines specific neural network architectures and configuration parameters for the density and texture (color) networks within Neural Scene Vector Fields ([NSVF](#7144-neural-sparse-voxel-fields-nsvf.md)) and related radiance field models [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the problem of how to structure the input features (position, direction, embeddings) and the network topology to optimize reconstruction quality and training stability. It sets itself apart from general [training loops](#4290-training-loop.md) by focusing on the internal MLP structure and feature concatenation strategies rather than the [optimization schedule](#3154-training-schedule.md) or ray sampling strategy.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves configuring two primary Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs): a density network and a texture (color) network. The inputs to these networks are constructed from [positional encodings](#876-positional-encoding.md), view directions, and optional appearance or voxel embeddings. The specific connection between feature layers and skip connections is configurable to balance capacity and convergence.

## Subtopics

### [Mip-NeRF 360](3306-mip-nerf-360.md)
[Mip-NeRF 360](#3306-mip-nerf-360.md) extends the quality of [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) to unbounded scenes where the camera may rotate 360 degrees and content exists at arbitrary distances. It sets itself apart from its parent [NeRF Training Loop](970-nerf-training-loop.md) and sibling [Mip-NeRF](link-to-mip-nerf) by combining a non-linear scene parameterization (contract mapping) to handle infinite space, anti-aliasing via cone-casting to resolve multi-scale details, and online distillation using a proposal network to maintain [training efficiency](#9264-optimization-and-training-efficiency.md) despite increased model capacity. See [Mip-NeRF 360](3306-mip-nerf-360.md).

### [NeRF-FF](8669-nerf-ff.md)
[NeRF-FF](#8669-nerf-ff.md) is a plug-in strategy that mitigates the degradation of [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) reconstruction quality caused by out-of-focus (defocus blurred) regions in input images. It operates by estimating binary image masks that identify in-focus regions, allowing a subsequently trained [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) model to omit out-of-focus pixels during training. Unlike methods that use dynamic ray generation or blur kernels (e.g., PDRF, Deblur-NeRF), NeRF-FF relies on static ray assumptions, making it compatible with runtime-optimized NeRF variants like [Instant-NGP](#6604-instant-ngp.md), nerfacto, and splatfacto. See [NeRF-FF](8669-nerf-ff.md).

### [Drone-NeRF](8972-drone-nerf.md)
[Drone-NeRF](#8972-drone-nerf.md) is a specialized volume rendering method for reconstructing large-scale 3D scenes from aerial drone imagery, addressing the challenges of unbounded space representation and varying camera exposure. It distinguishes itself from [standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) by integrating view frustum sampling for anti-aliasing, a pose optimizer for joint pose refinement, and appearance embeddings to handle exposure discrepancies, while employing a spatial contraction function to map unbounded scenes into a bounded domain for efficient rendering. It builds on [Specific Model Architectures and Extensions](10278-specific-model-architectures-and-extensions.md) by adding block-parallel training and shadow mitigation during the merging phase. See [Drone-NeRF](8972-drone-nerf.md).

#### ReconFusion
ReconFusion uses a Diffusion Prior to constrain unobserved views during reconstruction [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The NSVF (Neural Scene Vector Fields) framework was introduced by Facebook Research (Meta) as a method for neural scene representation [S1, unofficial]. The specific architecture variants (e.g., `nsvf_xyzn_old`, `nsvf_emb0`) are configurations within this framework that define how input features are mapped to density and color outputs. These configurations allow for experimentation with different input feature sets (such as voxel embeddings vs. raw coordinates) and network depths.
